slides.title: Good examples should teach usable next steps.
slides.notes:
The goal is reliable smaller steps, then useful delegation. TextCraft checks the final inventory and quantities.

The new lead is repairing what the learner sees before a correct action. The results here are not a test of learned recursion.

slides.title: Introduce a part before asking about it.
slides.notes:
SFT means supervised fine-tuning: copy a demonstrated next action. The diagram is simplified.

The repair changes histories, not 366 answers or 23 training steps. Answer tokens are matched; input length and computation are not. It still uses a known correct action list.

slides.title: The repair helped in three small comparisons.
slides.notes:
All models get 23 training steps. Counts are 1 to 14, 2 to 13, and 3 to 17, out of 32. The first two rows share goals; the third adds eight.

A randomized repair also helped. Neither clearly beat discovery. More training partly rescues the original teacher. These panels are exploratory.

slides.title: Reward training showed little transfer.
slides.notes:
One reward-training step per setting. Familiar: 9 to 13 and 14 to 16. Different goals: 4 to 5 and 5 to 5.

Eight different target roots, same recipe world; not held-out confirmation. The raw gain is one attempt. Fresh-A learning and extra SFT remain pending. Only this slide advances to 05:30 UTC.

slides.title: Next, test transfer and the value of one helper.
slides.notes:
We will test the repair in Phi, a second model family.

A helper completed a subtask, but screening ended before whole-task assessment. Next: working alone, or one helper chosen by fixed or adaptive rules. All share 96 calls and 8,192 output tokens, with no extra child budget.
